body:
A 50 lb bag of thinset covers about 90 sq ft with a small notch trowel and about 45 sq ft with a large one, so trowel size decides your bag count. For a 200 sq ft floor with large tile, plan on 5 bags before waste, and 6 bags in the cart. This guide shows the maker charts, the formula, and how to check your own floor.

## The formula and the coverage charts

**Bags = area in sq ft / coverage in sq ft per 50 lb bag for your trowel.**

Always divide by the low end of the chart range. Floors are not flat, tile backs are not smooth, and a mid-job store run costs more time than one spare bag.

Mapei lists this coverage for a 50 lb bag of its large tile and stone mortar.

| Trowel notch | Coverage per 50 lb bag |
| --- | --- |
| 1/4 x 1/4 x 1/4 in | 85 to 95 sq ft |
| 1/4 x 3/8 x 1/4 in | 65 to 75 sq ft |
| 1/2 x 1/2 x 1/2 in | 40 to 50 sq ft |
| 3/4 x 9/16 x 3/8 in U-notch | 35 to 40 sq ft |

Custom Building Products lists similar figures for VersaBond LFT. Its chart gives 85 to 95 sq ft at a 1/4 in square notch, 60 to 67 sq ft at a 1/4 x 3/8 in notch, 42 to 47 sq ft at a 1/2 in square notch, and 34 to 38 sq ft at a 3/4 in U-notch. The two makers agree within a few square feet, which makes the low ends safe planning numbers.

Match the notch to the tile. As a plain rule from the Custom chart, tile with a longest side under 8 in uses a 1/4 in square notch. Tile 8 to 15 in uses a 1/4 x 3/8 in notch. Tile over 15 in uses a 1/2 in square notch or a 3/4 in U-notch, plus back-buttering on large pieces.

Get your tile area first with our [tile calculator](/blog/tile-calculator/). It gives the sq ft and the box count. Use the same area here, before waste, then handle waste in the bag math below.

## Worked example: a 200 sq ft floor with 12 x 24 in tile

Your room is 10 x 20 ft (3.0 x 6.1 m), so the floor is 200 sq ft. The tile is 12 x 24 in porcelain, a large format tile. You choose a 1/2 x 1/2 in square notch trowel and plan to back-butter each tile.

Step 1: Area = 10 x 20 = 200 sq ft.

Step 2: Coverage at the low end for a 1/2 in notch on the Mapei chart = 40 sq ft per bag.

Step 3: Bags for the floor bed = 200 / 40 = 5 bags.

Step 4: Add waste and back-buttering. Back-buttering and cuts use extra mortar, so add 10 percent. 5 x 1.10 = 5.5 bags.

Step 5: Round up like a buyer. Buy 6 bags of 50 lb thinset.

Check the math a second way with the Custom chart. Its low end at a 1/2 in notch is 42 sq ft per bag. 200 / 42 = 4.76 bags. With 10 percent added, 4.76 x 1.10 = 5.24 bags, which still rounds up to 6 bags in the cart if you want a full spare, or 5 bags plus a small margin risk. We advise 6. Running out with half a tile bed open is the worse outcome.

If the same 200 sq ft floor used 6 in tile and a 1/4 in notch, the count drops hard. 200 / 85 = 2.35 bags, plus 10 percent is 2.59, rounded up to 3 bags. Same room, half the mortar. That is why a bag count without a trowel size means nothing.

## How to pick the right trowel

Lift a freshly set tile now and then as you work. The back should show near full contact, with the ridges flattened. Dry areas mean the notch is too small or the trowel angle is too low. Hold the trowel at about 45 degrees so the notches keep full depth.

Custom notes a minimum of 80 percent contact for dry areas and 95 percent for wet areas and exteriors. Large tile, warped tile, and stone need back-buttering to reach that contact. Budget the extra mortar, as in the example above.

For the joints that follow, use our [grout calculator](/blog/grout-calculator/) once tile size and joint width are fixed. Grout and thinset are bought on the same trip for most jobs.

## What changes how much thinset you use

Substrate flatness changes use more than most people expect. A dip filled with thinset can eat a quarter bag in a few square feet. Thinset is not a leveling product. Fix dips over about 1/4 in with a patch or self-leveler first.

Tile back pattern matters. Deep ridges and rough stone backs hold extra mortar. Mosaic on mesh often uses a smaller V-notch trowel, which spreads thinner and covers more area per bag.

Mixing waste is real. Mortar past its pot life must be thrown out, not retempered with extra water. Mapei lists a pot life of about 4 hours for its large tile mortar, and hot rooms cut that time. Mix half bags on small jobs. Plan your [flooring calculator](/blog/flooring-calculator/) run and your mortar run together so tile, thinset, and grout arrive in one trip.

## Mistakes that cost bags and tiles

The first mistake is a small notch on large tile to save mortar. Contact is poor, and tiles crack or sound hollow later. The saving is one bag. The repair is a floor.

The second mistake is spreading too large an area at once. Thinset skins over, often in 20 to 30 minutes in a warm room, and skinned mortar does not bond. Spread only what you can set in 10 to 15 minutes until you know your pace.

The third mistake is one mortar for every surface. Use modified mortar where the maker requires it, such as over plywood or for porcelain, and unmodified where a membrane maker requires it. The bag and the membrane sheet decide this.

The fourth mistake is no spare bag. One bad mix can end a Saturday job. A spare unopened bag can go back to the store.

## Frequently asked questions

### How many square feet does a 50 lb bag of thinset cover?
It depends on the notch. Maker charts list 85 to 95 sq ft with a 1/4 in square notch, 60 to 75 sq ft with a 1/4 x 3/8 in notch, and 40 to 50 sq ft with a 1/2 in square notch. Plan on the low end of each range.

### How much thinset do I need for 100 sq ft?
With a 1/4 x 3/8 in notch at 60 sq ft per bag, 100 sq ft needs 1.67 bags, rounded up to 2 bags. With a 1/2 in notch at 40 sq ft per bag, the same area needs 2.5 bags, rounded up to 3 bags.

### Do I need to back-butter large tile?
Yes, for tile with a side over 15 in, and for most 12 x 24 in floor tile. A thin skim on the tile back fills the ridges and helps reach full contact. Add about 10 percent more mortar to your bag count when you back-butter every piece.

### Can I use thinset to level a floor?
No, not for real dips. Thinset beds are thin by design, and thick beds shrink and bond poorly. Fill low spots with a patch compound or a self-leveler, let it cure, then tile over it at the normal bed depth.

### How long does mixed thinset last in the bucket?
Mapei lists about 4 hours of pot life for its large tile mortar at normal room temperature and humidity. Heat and sun cut that time. If the mortar stiffens, mix a fresh batch rather than adding water and stirring it back to life.

## Next step
